minutes.headline: Finance Committee discussed how to open up its budget process and agreed to write the Selectmen asking for a service-level meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee welcomed two new members, then spent most of the meeting on how it reviews budgets, the financial policies, new growth, school enrollment pressure and getting earlier information from the school and town sides. A member reported on a Massachusetts Municipal Association legislative update, and liaison updates were shared. Minutes of two earlier meetings were taken up, but the result of the vote is not in the captions.

public_comment.topic: A speaker asked that the committee schedule a meeting with the Town Manager before budget season to share the committee's suggestions on process.
Public service announcement: Memorial Day services Monday May 27th, 10 a.m., moving to the Senior Center if the weather is bad.

votes.motion: Motion and second for the chair to write a letter to the Board of Selectmen requesting a service-level or all-department meeting
Approve minutes of March 21, 2018 and May 7, 2018 with corrections (motion and second made)

budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed a rough proxy for population growth from new growth over recent years and the idea of a policy splitting new growth between schools and town.
A member said the OPEB overhang is an unfunded mandate that new school hires could worsen, with health insurance sitting on the town side.

budget_items.topic: State lottery and community impact fee
budget_items.what_was_said: A member reported expected state surplus and a community impact fee on marijuana sales that requires tracking related expenses.
A member raised an FCC proposal that could treat cable in-kind contributions as franchise fees under a cap, a possible hit to the public access budget.
The Council on Aging is on or slightly under budget, partly because meals-on-wheels drivers do not claim mileage.

decisions.decision: The chair will write a letter to the Board of Selectmen requesting a service-level or all-department meeting.
Members agreed in principle to seek a workshop-style meeting with the Town Manager before budget season.
Next meeting June 13th; whether to meet June 27th to be decided then.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee moved and seconded a motion for the chair to write the Board of Selectmen requesting a service-level, all-department meeting; the vote was not audible.
Members agreed in principle to seek a workshop-style meeting with the Town Manager before budget season, after a speaker in public comment asked for one.
Most of the meeting was discussion of the committee's role, financial policies, new growth, school enrollment pressure and earlier information from school and town sides.
A member raised OPEB costs and health insurance, and a possible federal change to how cable in-kind contributions count as franchise fees.
Minutes of two earlier meetings were taken up on a motion and second, but the result is not in the captions.

why_it_matters: The committee reviews budgets before Town Meeting, so an earlier, department-by-department look at services could change what residents see in the budget they are asked to vote on.
Unfunded retiree health costs, health insurance and possible cable fee changes are pressures that act on the town budget, mostly taxes, and on the public access budget.
